sam_new: Hey everyone, first week question. I'm trying to run embedding batches against the API from my laptop and getting intermittent 429s. I thought sandbox was fine for embeddings testing? :thinking:

rachel_devex: Welcome, Sam! :tada: Sandbox keys are fine for lightweight work but they have both QPS and daily token quotas. Embeddings can use a lot of tokens if you're sending big docs or batching a lot. Which key are you using (label/id)?

sam_new: It's the key named `sam-onboard-1` from the onboarding page. My script does 3 parallel requests each sending ~2k tokens per request, repeated in a loop. Response headers show `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0` sometimes and `x-quota-daily-remaining: 45900` other times. Confusing.

tony_infra: A couple things: sandbox enforcements include short-term QPS windows (requests/sec) and a daily token allotment. Hitting `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0` usually means you exceeded the per-second window; `x-quota-daily-remaining` is the daily token budget. They are separate. Also parallel short requests are more likely to trip QPS.

sam_new: Ah ok. Is there a Console view to see both windows in one place?

rachel_devex: Yes: Console -> Usage -> Keys will show per-key QPS windows and daily token usage. We also log recent client IPs and user agents so you can see if your CI picked up the key by accident. For quick header inspection try: ```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
``` Look for headers like `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`, `x-ratelimit-reset`, and `x-quota-daily-remaining`.

sam_new: Got it. I did the curl and saw `x-ratelimit-limit: 10`, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `x-ratelimit-reset: 6`. So I guess my parallelism is the problem. Any recommended client-side pattern for batch embedding tests?

tony_infra: For embeddings prefer batching tokens into fewer requests rather than many small ones. Also use a concurrency limiter (semaphore) and backoff. Example pseudo: ```py
# limit to N concurrent requests
semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(2)
async with semaphore:
  await call_embeddings(batch)
``` That keeps you under QPS.

rachel_devex: If you need a short demo spike we can grant a short sandbox boost. We require: key id, UTC start/end, expected rps, reason. Ping `devex-bot` with that template and it will create a ticket. We typically offer 10-30 minute demo bursts.

sam_new: I actually have a theater demo showing 50 small embeddings concurrently for 5 minutes on Tue at 17:00 UTC. Will that be possible?

rachel_devex: 50 concurrent small embeddings will be heavy. Better approach: show one request with a larger batch or precompute embeddings and replay results for the demo. If you really need live generation we can request a demo bump but we'll likely ask you to reduce concurrency (e.g., 10 rps sustained) or use a dedicated demo sandbox managed by DevEx.

devex-bot: Demo boost template: `key_id, 2026-05-12T17:00Z -> 2026-05-12T17:10Z, expected_rps, reason`. Example: `sam-onboard-1, 2026-05-12T17:00Z -> 2026-05-12T17:05Z, 20rps, onboarding demo`. Please DM or post here and we'll queue it.

sam_new: Thanks  I'll DM the template. Quick followup: do sandbox keys share quotas across an org or are they per-user? I don't want my tests to impact others in the company.

tony_infra: Sandbox keys are per-user and isolated from hosted capacity. Hosted/billed keys are account-level and can be shared depending on org settings. If you need team-wide testing, ask DevEx for a shared demo sandbox which we provision separately.

sam_new: Great, that eases my mind. One last tiny thing: my local CI pipeline accidentally uploaded the key to a public gist earlier. Anything I should do besides rotating the key?

rachel_devex: Rotate immediately and revoke the compromised key via Console -> API keys. Also check Console -> Usage to see if there were unexpected spikes (client IPs). If you need a replacement key flagged as "onboard" just ask and we'll issue one.

ci-bot: Security reminder: do not commit API keys to public repos. See internal docs at https://intranet.redwood.ai/security/keys for best practices.

sam_new: Done rotating and removed the gist. Appreciate the quick help and tips! :pray:
